policy: Apify Store Publishing Terms section 9.4 (verified); the brief cited 2.2.4.2, which is "Specific Prohibitions".
changeLimit: At most 1 price-increasing change per month per Actor; a pending change cannot be cancelled or edited.
reasonForChange: Consolidation of single-source Actors into global-corporate-patent-intelligence: each legacy source keeps its own per-record price as a separate event, and the start event is set to $0.005.

ratifiedEvents.name: uae-entity-updated
ratifiedEvents.rationale: Rule R-LOW: the router cannot tell a status change from any other update, so the LOWER documented legacy rate is used and no caller pays more for an update than the legacy actor charged (status change $0.02, content change $0.01, uae-corporate-registry-monitor/README.md:174-175).
ratifiedEvents.reviewWhen: After 90 days of production deltas: if status changes are more than 25 percent of this source's updated rows, split the event in two (a new paid event needs the 14-day notice of Terms 9.4); otherwise keep it.

ratifiedEvents.name: watchlist-hit
ratifiedEvents.rationale: Locked at $0.15 per matched record in all three engines. Evidence: the live price of the same event on the legacy Actors on 2026-10-17 (public Apify API, anonymous; extracted by the owner's suite into data/fleet_contracts.json, not part of this repository) was $0.15 for sec-enforcement-litigation-delta-feed and clinicaltrials-orange-book-delta, $0.12 for ai-crawler-content-signal-permission-monitor, $0.10 for regione-lombardia-grants-registry-monitor and singapore-acra-registry-monitor. $0.15 is the highest of them and one rule for three engines; the tender engine's only watchlist source (Lombardia) therefore rises from $0.10 to $0.15. A hit is charged once, after the row event was billed and the delivery journal written, and only for a valid keyword (>= 2 alphanumerics); the default caps (200 hits and $50 per run) bound the exposure (docs/audits/2026-10-21_pricing_exposure.md).
ratifiedEvents.reviewWhen: After 30 days or at the first customer complaint about hits: a decrease is immediate, an increase needs 14 days of notice, so the lower value is the cheaper one to try if conversion is poor.

startPriceRatification.decidedBy: delegate of the owner under the owner's mandate of 2026-11-02 (authority to settle G1 to G5)
startPriceRatification.rationale: Locked at $0.005 per started GB of memory (regtech 2,048 MB = 2 events = $0.01 per run; tenders and patents 1,024 MB = $0.005). Infrastructure: the marketplace keeps 20 percent, so one start event nets $0.004, which pays for 72 seconds of one GB of compute at $0.20 per GB-hour and 36 seconds at $0.40 (net / rate x 3600), the least a run costs that boots a container and fetches one page. Market: in the public Store sample of 2026-10-17 (692 listings with a start event, popularity-biased) $0.005 is at the 65th percentile (405 listings below, 97 equal, 190 above); 287 of 692 (41.5 percent) charge $0.005 or more and 288 (41.6 percent) keep the platform default of $0.00005; the median of the 30-day users is 20 for listings at $0.005 or more and 18 at the default (descriptive, no causal claim). The operator-requested range is $0.002 to $0.01.
startPriceRatification.reviewWhen: After 30 days of runs, compare the median billed run time with 36 to 72 seconds per GB: a start fee that over-recovers can be lowered at once; an increase needs 14 days of notice (Terms 9.4) and counts as the month's one price-raising change.

notes: The default apify-actor-start price is $0.00005; 0.005 is 100x that. Apify only recommends keeping the default; it documents no maximum.
With 1024 MB the start event is charged 1 time(s) per run = $0.005, even when a run delivers no records.
apify-default-dataset-item is intentionally absent: with it priced, pushData(item, eventName) bills both events per row.
startedAt must be re-computed from the real submission time before sending; regenerate with --now=<ISO instant>.
